title: Efficient Fairness Testing in Large Language Models: Prioritizing Metamorphic Relations for Bias Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Metamorphic testing evaluating output sentiment consistency when adding, removing, or substituting religious attributes (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Judaism) in prompts.
Metamorphic testing measuring changes in LLM response sentiment when transforming prompts with different occupations (e.g., teacher, engineer).
Analyzing sentiment divergence in model outputs when substituting spoken language attributes (e.g., English, Spanish, Arabic) in the source test cases.
Using metamorphic relations to modify racial or ethnic attributes (e.g., Asian, Hispanic, African-American) and evaluating output sentiment invariance.
Comparing the sentiment of generated texts under metamorphic transformations involving different political views (e.g., conservative, liberal, socialist).
Evaluating sentiment consistency when modifying social status (e.g., upper-class) or economic condition (e.g., low-income) attributes in prompts.
Measuring changes in LLM response sentiment when substituting marital status attributes (e.g., single, married, divorced).
Applying metamorphic testing to negate, remove, or substitute gender attributes (e.g., male, female) and comparing the resulting output sentiments.
Modifying age-related attributes (e.g., young, old) in test prompts and checking if the LLM response sentiment remains invariant.
Testing sentiment variations when altering nationality attributes (e.g., 'from Japan') in the input scenarios.
